learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to solve thermodynamic problems with logical solutions, not by rote.
Students will be able to calculate thermodynamic properties such as enthalpy, entropy, fugacity, and activity coefficient for pure substances or solutions under single/multi-phase conditions.
Students will be able to draw P-x, P-y graphs for a binary system.
Students will be able to solve phase equilibrium problems.
Students will be able to determine the equilibrium compositions of chemically reacting mixtures.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics, Basic concepts
Volumetric properties of pure liquids, Equations of state
Heat effects: Sensible heat effects, Standard heat of reaction
Thermodynamic properties of fluids: Basic property relations, Residual Properties, Thermodynamic diagrams

Solution thermodynamics, Relations between basic properties, Partial properties, Gibbs Duhem equation, Ideal gas mixtures, Fugacity and fugacity coefficient in pure and mixture states, Ideal solution, Difference properties
Solution thermodynamics: Fugacity and fugacity coefficient in pure and mixture states, Ideal solution, Difference properties
Applications of solution thermodynamics, Activity coefficient, Lewis Randall rule, Gibbs free energy difference, Property changes due to mixing, Heat of mixing
Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium: Raoult's law, Modified Raoult's law
Vapor-liquid equilibrium: Liquid activity coefficient correlations, K value correlations, Flash calculations
Chemical reaction equilibrium: Equilibrium reactions, Van't Hoff equation
Chemical reaction equilibrium: Concentration dependence of the equilibrium constant
bibliography: J. M. Smith, H. C. Van Ness, M. M. Abbott, Introduction to Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics 7e (The Mcgraw-Hill Chemical Engineering Series)
S. I. Sandler, Chemical, Biochemical and Engineering Thermodynamics, 4th Edition, Wiley, 2006.
Çengel, Yunus A., “Introduction to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer”, McGraw_Hill, 1997.
